cards.back: A bookkeeping assignment: valence electrons minus nonbonding electrons minus half the bonding electrons.
A vector measure of separated positive and negative charge in a bond or molecule.
The reactant consumed first under the balanced stoichiometric ratio; it limits theoretical product.
Moles of solute divided by final solution volume in liters.
A property whose change depends only on initial and final states, not the path taken.
Reaction enthalpies add when chemical equations are added, because enthalpy is a state function.
The mass-action expression evaluated at the current composition.
The value of the reaction quotient at equilibrium for a specified temperature and standard-state convention.
m = c × V × M; divide by purity; use the hydrate molar mass if weighing a hydrate.
C₁V₁ = C₂V₂; make up to the final volume rather than adding the full volume of solvent.
Total factor is the product of step factors; random errors add in quadrature, systematic errors compound.
For products and quotients, relative errors add in quadrature; the largest relative error dominates.
Polar bonds plus asymmetric geometry give a net dipole: water polar (bent), CO₂ nonpolar (linear).
K_ow = [octanol]/[water]; amount fraction in water = V_w/(V_w + K V_o).
q_soln = m c ΔT; q_rxn = −q_soln; ΔH = q_rxn/n.
Endothermic dissolution: solubility rises with T; exothermic (most gases): falls.
Z counts protons, A−Z counts neutrons and ionic charge adjusts electron count; changing electrons does not change element identity.
N=nN_A counts specified entities; the same amount can correspond to different masses for different substances.
In vacuum E=hc/λ. Convert wavelength to matching units and distinguish per-photon from per-mole energy.
Defining constants are exact; measured wavelength, amount and composition still limit uncertainty and reported figures.
Add valence electrons and adjust for ionic charge; formal charges must sum to the net species charge.
Electron-domain geometry includes lone pairs; molecular shape describes atom positions. A multiple bond is one VSEPR direction.
Bond dipoles are vectors; equal opposing dipoles can cancel despite polar individual bonds.
Interaction labels and qualitative solubility rules do not by themselves establish a measured material property.
n_i=n_i,0+ν_iξ with signed coefficients; all reactant amounts must remain nonnegative.
Percent yield is recovered target mass divided by theoretical mass times 100; composition and recovery assumptions matter.
Perform reaction amount accounting before dividing by final mixture volume.
A net ionic equation omits spectators from the reaction, not from full charge balance; completion needs justification.
PV=nRT uses absolute temperature and a gas constant compatible with pressure and volume units.
p_i=y_iP with y_i=n_i/n_total; mass fraction is generally different from mole fraction.
u_rms=√(3RT/M) uses kg/mol with SI R and is not a directed bulk velocity.
Z=PV/(nRT)=1 for the ideal model; a mismatch alone does not uniquely identify a real-gas mechanism.
ΔU=q+w with heat entering and work done on the system positive; expansion work is −P_extΔV.
Reaction heat is minus all modeled surroundings heat; include stated solution and calorimeter heat capacities.
Add compatible reaction enthalpies, reverse signs when reversing equations and scale energies with coefficients.
U and H are state functions; q and w depend on the path. Phase and work assumptions matter.
Combine the equilibrium relation with conserved amounts and reject inadmissible negative roots.
Reversing a reaction inverts K; doubling all coefficients squares it under the same conditions.
Thermodynamic quotients use dimensionless activities; raw concentration ratios cancel units only in suitable stoichiometries.
K constrains equilibrium composition, not approach time. A catalyst changes rates without changing K at fixed conditions.
pH=−log₁₀a_H; a concentration calculation requires declared normalization and ideal/activity assumptions.
Strong-acid equivalents reduce A⁻ and increase HA before a valid buffer-ratio approximation is applied.
A zero or negative formal base inventory invalidates the buffer logarithm; use mass/equilibrium/charge balance.
Reference calibration and independent composition information test different explanations; neither alone validates every nonideal effect.
Reported reference mean minus stipulated target gives the common additive pH offset in this construction.
Update acid/base inventories first; zero or negative nominal base invalidates the buffer-ratio logarithm.
Calibration constrains reporting bias; independently supplied composition tests chemical inventory. Neither alone establishes every real effect.
Arithmetic mean pH and minus log of mean hydrogen concentration are generally different quantities.
The outer-shell electron configuration helps predict main-group valence patterns; it is an occupancy model, not a classical electron path.
Across a period, rising effective nuclear charge generally contracts radius; down a group, added shells generally increase it. Check subshell and pairing exceptions.
Bond order is one half of bonding minus antibonding electrons. Removing an antibonding electron raises the simple-model bond order by one half.
In the stated models, π(2p) is below σ(2p) for N₂; σ(2p) is below π(2p) for O₂. Use the appropriate ordering before filling electrons.
Two unpaired electrons in separate equal-energy π* orbitals make the stated O₂ model paramagnetic; N₂ has paired occupancy.
Qualitative orbital occupancy supports bond-order and unpaired-electron reasoning; it does not supply exact orbital energies or bond-dissociation energies.
Steric number 2, 3, 4 → sp, sp², sp³; angles 180°, 120°, 109.47°; s-character 50%, 33.3%, 25%. Hybrid count equals the number of atomic orbitals mixed.
Single: 1σ. Double: 1σ + 1π. Triple: 1σ + 2π. π overlap is side by side, so double bonds resist rotation.
For equivalent s + λp hybrids, cos θ = −1/λ² and s-character = 1/(1 + λ²). Smaller angles mean more p-character in the bonds and more s in lone pairs (Bent's rule).
Hybrids describe a known geometry; they do not explain O₂ paramagnetism or delocalization, and sp³d/sp³d² pictures are poor for main-group atoms.

cards.front: How is an extent domain obtained for A ⇌ 2B?
cards.back: Require n_A,0−ξ≥0 and n_B,0+2ξ≥0 together, giving −n_B,0/2≤ξ≤n_A,0. The initial quotient then selects a direction within that domain.

cards.front: Why does beta not cancel completely for A ⇌ 2B?
cards.back: There are two product activity factors and one reactant activity factor, leaving one beta. Omitting it changes the numerical quotient and its convention.

cards.front: What checks must follow a numerical equilibrium root?
cards.back: Check every amount is nonnegative, the conserved-unit ledger closes, and the original activity expression returns K. Algebra alone does not select a physical model state.

cards.front: Why must a heat statement name its boundary even after ΔH is known?
cards.back: Enthalpy is a state-function change; heat is a transfer. At constant pressure with only pressure-volume work they coincide, but fixed temperature by itself is insufficient.

cards.front: Does a correct equilibrium composition determine reaction rate or a laboratory method?
cards.back: No. It constrains a state under a declared model. Kinetic parameters, species identity and physical conditions require separate information.

cards.front: How are photon and ionization energies defined?
cards.back: As positive differences between the specified initial and final energy levels,with their reference and model stated.

cards.front: Why can radial probability peak away from the nucleus?
cards.back: The radial measure includes spherical-shell volume;it differs from probability density per volume.

cards.front: Which objects must be distinguished in electron counting?
cards.back: One orbital,a subshell and an entire shell,with spin capacity reported separately from spatial-state count.

cards.front: What distinguishes an internal model check from experimental validation?
cards.back: Normalization and equation agreement test the declared model;measured observables and its omitted physics require separate evidence.

cards.front: Why does overlap appear in the energy equation?
cards.back: Projection uses the overlap matrix as well as the Hamiltonian;normalization and eigenvalues depend on that declared basis.

cards.front: Why cannot overlapping basis coefficient squares simply be added?
cards.back: Their spatial cross term contributes to the total norm;individual coefficients are not independent probabilities.

cards.front: What is required for an energy comparison?
cards.back: An explicit particle-matched reference and consistent included energy terms,plus a clear statement of omitted physics.

cards.front: Why keep bond order and energy distinct?
cards.back: An occupancy indicator summarizes one model feature;energy differences require explicit states,references and included interactions.

cards.front: What prevents a level value from being mistaken for a photon energy?
cards.back: Draw the signed reference and both levels,then compute the specified positive difference.

cards.front: Which independent checks support a cumulative probability?
cards.back: Its defining integral,derivative,zero/large-radius limits and bounds between zero and one.

cards.front: How can the energy calculation be checked independently?
cards.back: Substitute into both projected equations and the determinant condition,using the same overlap and phase convention.

cards.front: Why is a particle-matched reference necessary but insufficient?
cards.back: It fixes the accounting comparison while leaving omitted physical energy terms and experimental validation unresolved.

cards.front: Which reaction quantities can change while atoms are conserved?
cards.back: Individual species amounts,total molecule count and pressure can change;the correctly weighted atom invariant remains fixed.

cards.front: What belongs next to every reaction-heat result?
cards.back: The system boundary,mechanical constraint,sign convention and included work/energy terms.

cards.front: What must accompany a calibration correction?
cards.back: Its measurement model and shared-error assumptions,plus independent evidence if stronger specificity or stability claims are sought.

cards.front: What makes a cumulative ledger coherent?
cards.back: Use the same declared state,reference,feasible domain and mechanical boundary across amount,pressure,equilibrium and energy checks.

One photon ejects one electron: KE_max = hν − φ = hc/λ − φ, and eV_s = KE_max. No emission below ν₀ = φ/h, however intense the light. Intensity sets how many electrons leave; frequency sets their maximum energy. E[eV] = 1239.84/λ[nm].

λ = h/p = h/(mv). Accelerated through V: λ = h/√(2meV), which is 0.123 nm at 100 V. Macroscopic objects have negligible wavelengths. Δx Δp ≥ ħ/2 limits the position and momentum a wave-like state can have at once; it is not an instrument limit.
Standing waves fit L = nλ/2 with n = 1, 2, 3, …, so E_n = n²h²/(8mL²). The lowest energy E₁ is not zero, the gaps (2n + 1)E₁ grow, and E ∝ 1/L². Probability in 0 to a: a/L − sin(2nπa/L)/(2nπ).

h, c and e are exact; the electron mass is measured. Use hc = 1239.84 eV·nm for photons, 1 eV = 1.602 × 10⁻¹⁹ J, and metres in h²/(8mL²). A 1 nm box gives E₁ near 0.38 eV. Box levels go as n², hydrogenic levels as −1/n². The treatment is non-relativistic.

Total valence electrons (minus the charge of a cation, plus the charge of an anion), then single bonds, octets on terminal atoms, leftovers on the central atom, and formal charges that sum to the net charge. An odd total leaves an unpaired electron.

Incomplete octet: B in BF₃ has 6 electrons and is a Lewis acid. Odd-electron radical: NO₂ has 17 electrons and one unpaired. Expanded valence: period-3 and heavier centres (SF₆ 12 electrons, PCl₅ 10, XeF₄ 12). C, N, O and F stay at 8.

Steric number 5 (trigonal bipyramid; lone pairs equatorial): 0 lone pairs PCl₅, 1 see-saw SF₄, 2 T-shaped ClF₃, 3 linear XeF₂. Steric number 6 (octahedron): 0 SF₆, 1 square pyramidal BrF₅, 2 square planar XeF₄ and ICl₄⁻. Angles 90°, 120°, 180°.

Formal charge = valence electrons − nonbonding electrons − half the bonding electrons. Sulfate with four single bonds has S +2; with two S=O it has S 0. Both drawings give the same shape. Neither measures real charge or proves d-orbital participation.
